newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends stable on lack of direction.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends stable on lack of direction.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed little changed against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday as no factors emerged to give the local unit any trading direction, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.500 against Monday's T$27.499 close. Turnover through dealers was a modest US$192 million.
U.S. dollar demand emerged at the opening to push the Taiwan dollar slightly lower, but greenback selling soon emerged.
"Exporters entered to sell U.S. dollars quite actively, balancing the trade," said one dealer.
"Tuesday's trade was mainly routine commercial demand and supply. Investors have shown little interest in speculation amid a lack of direction," the dealer said.
In the absence of speculative forces, the Taiwan dollar usually trades in a stable, narrow range, he said.
A T$27.49-27.51 trading range was seen for Wednesday.
